findings.note: When --include-untracked is omitted, the implementation passes an invented --no-include-untracked argument instead of omitting the optional flag. This violates REQ-001/AC-004's verbatim pass-through contract and may be rejected by the upstream CLI.

The implementation iterates affected_components in the dependency-provided order and merely comments that it is already sorted. REQ-001 and REQ-005 require the Resolver itself to evaluate components in ascending lexicographic order and remain invariant to input ordering.

A WARN Block emits only one severity:block diagnostic. REQ-004/AC-056 require one severity:warn diagnostic per individual WARN evidence node plus exactly one severity:block summary; the tests currently encode the incomplete single-entry behavior.

A capability entry is appended only after all of that capability's trigger and conditional-facet evaluations finish. If a dependency fails mid-capability, evaluations already performed for that capability are discarded from Resolver Evidence, contrary to the requirement to record every evaluation actually performed.
